name: Uniform polygon second area moments
definition: For CCW simple polygon vertices (x_i,y_i) with cyclic indices, let c_i=x_i y_(i+1)−x_(i+1)y_i. Then M20=Σ_i c_i(x_i²+x_i x_(i+1)+x_(i+1)²)/12, M02=Σ_i c_i(y_i²+y_i y_(i+1)+y_(i+1)²)/12 and M11=Σ_i c_i(2x_i y_i+x_i y_(i+1)+x_(i+1)y_i+2x_(i+1)y_(i+1))/24.
variables: c_i oriented edge determinant; M20=∫_P x² dA, M02=∫_P y² dA, M11=∫_P xy dA; P polygon interior
assumptions: One simple counterclockwise polygonal boundary with positive area and finite coordinates; uniform unit area density; repeated closing vertex optional, no holes
limitations: O(n) arithmetic and O(1) auxiliary storage, excluding input validation. Raw origin-dependent moments have units of length to the fourth power, not normalized or central moments. The mixed moment can be negative; do not take its absolute value. Floating-point cancellation and overflow may occur with large coordinate offsets or near-degenerate polygons
failure_conditions: Self-intersecting or zero-area boundary, wrong orientation, nonfinite coordinates or unsupported holes.
computation: Accumulate the three signed edge sums in exact or suitably controlled arithmetic. Check positive signed area and valid simple boundary first; a reversed boundary negates all three sums. The coefficients follow by integrating degree-two monomials over oriented triangles with vertices at the origin and each edge endpoint.

source.citation: J. Burkardt, polygon_integrals (revised 11 January 2021), Florida State University-hosted documentation, low-order raw moment formulas, https://people.sc.fsu.edu/~jburkardt/m_src/polygon_integrals/polygon_integrals.html ; Bockman (1989) and Steger (1996) listed there, originals not reviewed.

mechanism_note: Diagnostic extending signed polygon area and first moments to raw quadratic integrals, not a new distinct algorithm. On a reference simplex the integrals of the squared barycentric coordinates are 1/12 and of their product 1/24; multiplying by the signed determinant and expanding the monomials gives the edge formulas. Oriented triangle chains sum to the polygon integral even when the origin is outside.

name: Affine lower envelope by monotone slope stack
definition: For lines f_i(x)=m_i x+b_i sorted by strictly decreasing slope after retaining the least intercept per slope, keep an envelope stack with increasing start breakpoints. For new line j and last line i, compute x_ij=(b_j−b_i)/(m_i−m_j); pop i if x_ij≤its start, and repeat; append j with its computed start or −∞ for the first line. Query the last start≤x to obtain min_i f_i(x).
variables: m_i slope; b_i intercept; x_ij crossing; x finite query; n input line count; h retained envelope line count
assumptions: Nonempty static set of finite affine functions on the entire real axis, exact ordered comparisons; only minimum value required, not every minimizing identity
limitations: O(n log(n+1)) sorting and O(n) stack work, O(n) storage, O(log(h+1)) query. Parallel lines with greater intercept are dominated; identical lines and isolated breakpoint-only ties need not retain their identities. No arbitrary insertion, deletion, vertical lines, bounded segments or floating-point robustness guarantee
failure_conditions: Empty input, nonfinite coefficients or query, failure to deduplicate slopes, or inexact intersection ordering.
computation: Keep the smallest intercept at each slope, process descending slopes, and maintain strictly increasing start breakpoints with an explicit negative-infinity sentinel. Remove a previous line when its crossing with the new line is at or before its own start. Binary-search the finite starts to find the active affine function.

source.citation: R. Wein, CGAL 6.2 2D Envelopes user manual, introduction and convex hull with envelopes example, https://doc.cgal.org/6.2/Envelope_2/index.html ; pointwise minimum and point-line duality reviewed. The slope-stack construction, tie rule and query bounds are independently derived here, not claimed to be CGAL's implementation.

required_inputs: Finite affine functions and query coordinate.
mechanism_note: Dual monotone convex-hull variant, not a new distinct algorithm: mapping a line to (m,−b) maps lower-envelope segments to the upper hull. A smaller-slope new line beats the last line to the right of their crossing; if that crossing is no later than the last line's start, the last line has no surviving interval. Otherwise the crossing is the new start. Each line is pushed and popped at most once, giving linear stack work.
